content.title: Watch live as President Trump addresses nation on Iran war
content.text: April 1, 2026, 8:00 p.m. ETPresident Donald Trump is set to deliver a primetime address to the nation on Wednesday, April 1, as the White House signals the United States may soon wind down its role in the Iran war.The 9 p.m. ET address comes amid Trump’s recent comments about a possible ceasefire and renewed threats to pull the United States out of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization. Trump told Reuters on April 1 that he expects the U.S. campaign in Iran to end "pretty quickly," adding that he is no longer concerned about Iran's enriched uranium because the facilities are buried deep underground and monitored by satellites.The president has repeatedly said preventing Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon was the war's top objective.Here's what to know about Trump's address and how to watch.What time is Trump's national address?Trump is expected to address the nation at 9 p.m. ET on Wednesday, April 1.Watch Trump's national address on Iran liveUSA TODAY is streaming Trump's address starting at 9 p.m. ET on April 1.The address is also expected to stream live on the White House's website and YouTube channel. The address is likely to air on every major network, including ABC, NBC, CBS, CNN, Fox News, and NewsNation.Why is Trump addressing the nation?The United States will end its war in Iran "fairly soon" and return only for limited strikes if needed, Trump told Reuters on Wednesday, April 1, just hours before his planned primetime address to the nation."Within two weeks, maybe, two weeks, maybe three," Trump told reporters March 31 in the Oval Office. "We can see the finish line," Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in a separate interview on Fox News' "Hannity."Trump also told Reuters he plans to announce during the 9 p.m. ET address that he is considering withdrawing the United States from NATO after some European members refused to send ships to help unblock the Strait of Hormuz.The president's decision to address the nation comes as public support for the conflict appears limited. About two-thirds of Americans say they want the administration to end the fighting, even if it means the United States does not achieve Trump's goals, according to a new Reuters/Ipsos poll.Saman Shafiq is a trending news reporter for USA TODAY. Reach her at sshafiq@usatodayco.com and follow her on X and Instagram @saman_shafiq7.
